pages.title: Banach-Tarski Sphere
pages.text: A solid sphere that can be cut into five non-measurable pieces and reassembled, by rotation alone, into two spheres the same size as the original. It relies on the axiom of choice, and the pieces have no well-defined volume. It is perfectly smooth and quietly unsettling.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Cantor Diagonalizer, I used an Aleph-Null Shard to choose a point from each of uncountably many orbits on a sphere. The choice split it into pieces, and when I put them back I had two.
